gapTheirs: No size hierarchy in headings: the H1 '# The Lighthouse' and the H2 '## What the sea keeps' both measure a 38-39px ink band — identical to the 38-39px band of body text. verdict: B is not a typographic choice, it is an absence of one — white type on off-white paper, where the only way I could read the passage was to push a 96-100% levels curve through the file. Every enrichment is gone with it: the asterisks around 'bottle' sit at the same weight and colour as the prose, so the markup is louder than the emphasis it marks. A gets the fundamentals right that B abandons — #1C1C1C ink, syntax marks recessed four steps to #9E9E9E so '#' and '*' fall out of the reading line, a 3px cyan caret at full 72px line height. A's own failure is that its headings only pretend to be headings: same cap height as body, same air above, bold and nothing else, which means at a glance a section break reads as a paragraph that happens to be emphasised.

states.name: quattro
states.gap: The ink is lighter than the paper: glyphs render #FFFFFF on a #F9F9F9 page — a contrast ratio of about 1.06:1, versus A's #1C1C1C on the same #F9F9F9 at roughly 14.6:1. Frame-wide maximum saturation is 4.3%, so there is no coloured caret either; the cursor is a near-white hairline against near-white, where A's is a 6px (3 CSS px) #00B5FF bar spanning the full 36 CSS px line.
states.gapTheirs: Headings defect to a proportional grotesque while body and italic stay mono, and the H2 gets no size step at all: H1 ascender-to-descender is 38px, H2 is 31px — identical to body's 31px. So '## What the sea keeps' is body-size, carried only by weight, and bold spans like 'bottle' render at a proportional advance inside a monospace line, breaking the character column mid-sentence. The italic, by contrast, is a true mono italic on the grid — so the family switch is inconsistent, not a policy.
states.verdict: B is not a typeface choice, it is an absence of one — white text on off-white, 1.06:1, invisible until I level-stretched the file to confirm there was a document under there at all. Even amplified it does nothing with the type: '##' and '**bottle**' sit at full body ink, same weight, same colour as the prose, so the markup is louder than the words and the structure is flat. A actually sets the passage — markers muted to about #B0B0B0, a real mono italic rather than a slanted roman, a caret you can find without hunting — but its heading logic is half-built: H2 is the same size as body text and the bold jumps to a proportional sans, so 'bottle' visibly falls off the monospace column that the rest of the line is standing on. Same 36 CSS px line pitch, same ~18px mono, same paper in both, so the rhythm is a wash; A wins on ink and on markdown weight, and loses nothing that would stop a writer typing.

states.name: mono
states.gap: Body ink is pure #FFFFFF on a #F9F9F9 ground — 1.05:1 contrast, i.e. white ink on near-white paper. Measured across the whole text column the minimum luminance is 249 (the only pixel below that in the entire file is the #959595 scrollbar). B's ink is #1C1C1C at 16.19:1. On top of that A applies zero styled rendering: h2 stroke coverage 0.151 vs body 0.141 over the identical string (+7% = the same regular weight), where B's h2 is 0.233 (+64%) and **bottle** is 0.267 (+88%); and A's '##', '**' and '-' are #FFFFFF, byte-identical to the prose, against B's #9E9E9E. No caret anywhere in frame either — an erode test for any 1px column with 50 consecutive near-white rows returns 0, while B has a 6x72px (3x36 CSS) #00B5FF bar.
states.gapTheirs: Ink is #1C1C1C — 16.19:1 on #F9F9F9, a hard screen-black that hammers at 20px/1.8 over a working session; ~#2E2E2E (≈11:1) is where a long-form surface should sit. And the recessive greys are not one value: '#'/'##'/'**' are #9E9E9E (2.54:1) but the list hyphen is #7A7A7A (4.0:1) — two different marker greys in the same left margin, so the bullets sit a step louder than the heading marks for no reason.
states.verdict: A is not a typographic choice, it is a broken colour token: #FFFFFF text on #F9F9F9 paper, 1.05:1, a page you can only read by tilting the screen. Everything downstream is dead with it — headings render at body weight, '##' and '**' carry exactly the same ink as the sentences they mark, and there is no caret in frame at all, so you cannot even find where you are typing. B is the same font at the same 20px/36px on the same 63ch measure, but it actually puts ink down: real bold on headings, a true cursive italic (single-storey 'a'), markers pushed back to #9E9E9E, and a 3px cyan caret standing the full line-height. B's own sins are real — near-black ink and h1, h2 and body all at the identical 39px ascender-to-descender band, so a '# ' and a '## ' produce visually identical lines — but that is a hierarchy argument, not a legibility one.
